name: PROJECT: AFFLUENTOS The Affluentaccelerators Internal Business

messages.content:
PROJECT: AFFLUENTOS

The Affluentaccelerators Internal Business Operations, CRM & Sales Management Platform

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

Build a full-stack, secure, multi-user internal business management web application called AffluentOS for The Affluentaccelerators.

AffluentOS is the central operating system for managing the company's business inquiries, customer relationships, sales activities, consulting engagements, team members, business development activities, and overall operational performance.

The platform should combine the functionality of:

- A Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system.
- A Sales Pipeline Management System.
- An Inquiry and Lead Management System.
- A Business Development Management System.
- A Client and Project Management System.
- A Team Assignment and Performance Management System.
- A Business Intelligence Dashboard.

The application will be used by the founder, administrators, business development managers, sales representatives, consultants, analysts, and other authorised team members.

The platform must support multiple users logging in with individual accounts and permissions.

It should be designed as a scalable internal company application rather than a basic data-entry dashboard.

Primary objective:

Centralise all company inquiries, contacts, opportunities, sales activities, consulting engagements, and team performance in one organised, accessible, and measurable system.

---

2. BRANDING AND USER INTERFACE

Application name: AffluentOS.

Parent organisation: The Affluentaccelerators.

Tagline: Your Business. Your People. Your Progress.

Design direction:

Create a premium SaaS-style business application interface.

The application should look like a modern CRM and enterprise operations platform.

Visual identity:

- Deep emerald green as the primary brand colour.
- White and off-white backgrounds.
- Dark charcoal text.
- Subtle gold accents.
- Light grey borders.
- Clean cards and data visualisations.

Design inspiration:

- HubSpot CRM.
- Attio.
- Pipedrive.
- Linear.
- Monday.com.

The interface should be sophisticated, intuitive, uncluttered, and easy to use.

Use:

- A collapsible left sidebar.
- A clean top navigation bar.
- Responsive dashboards.
- Tables with sorting and filtering.
- Searchable databases.
- Kanban boards.
- Interactive charts.
- Activity timelines.
- Status indicators.
- Contextual action menus.
- Modal forms and slide-out detail panels.

Prioritise desktop usability while ensuring that the application works excellently on mobile devices.

---

3. USER AUTHENTICATION AND ROLE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL

Create a secure authentication system.

Every team member should have an individual account.

Login requirements:

- Email and password authentication.
- Password reset.
- Secure session management.
- User profile.
- Profile picture.
- Account activation and deactivation.
- Last login information.

USER ROLES

Create the following default roles.

A. SUPER ADMIN / FOUNDER

Full platform access.

Permissions:

- Access all company data.
- View all inquiries and contacts.
- Create, edit, assign, and delete records where permitted.
- Manage all users.
- Assign roles and permissions.
- Monitor every BD manager and sales representative.
- View company-wide dashboards.
- Manage sales pipelines.
- Assign consultants and analysts.
- View all client engagements.
- Configure application settings.
- Access audit logs.
- Export company reports.

B. ADMINISTRATOR / OPERATIONS MANAGER

Permissions:

- Manage inquiries.
- Manage contacts.
- Assign leads.
- Manage team members within authorised scope.
- Coordinate consultants.
- Monitor activities.
- Update client engagement records.
- View operational reports.
- Manage relevant application data.

C. BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT MANAGER

Permissions:

- View assigned leads.
- Create new prospects and business contacts.
- Submit new client inquiries manually.
- Update lead statuses.
- Manage sales opportunities.
- Record calls, meetings, emails, and follow-ups.
- Add notes to contacts.
- Create deals.
- Update pipeline stages.
- Request consultant assignment.
- View personal sales performance.
- View authorised team pipeline information.

D. SALES REPRESENTATIVE

Permissions:

- Manage assigned prospects.
- Create new leads.
- Record sales activities.
- Update assigned opportunities.
- Schedule follow-ups.
- Submit proposals and quotations.
- Track conversion progress.
- View personal performance.

E. CONSULTANT / BUSINESS ANALYST

Permissions:

- View assigned consulting engagements.
- Access authorised client information.
- View client diagnostic documents.
- Update project progress.
- Submit analysis reports.
- Upload deliverables.
- Record project notes.
- Update task status.
- Communicate project progress internally.

F. TEAM MEMBER / FELLOW / INTERN

Permissions:

- Access specifically assigned projects and tasks.
- Update assigned task progress.
- Submit research and project reports.
- Upload authorised deliverables.
- View relevant team information.

IMPORTANT:

Implement proper role-based access control at the database level, not just by hiding buttons in the frontend.

Users must not be able to access unauthorised records by manipulating URLs or API requests.

Allow the super admin to customise permissions in the future.

---

4. MAIN APPLICATION NAVIGATION

Create the following sidebar structure:

1. Overview
2. Inquiries
3. CRM / Contacts
4. Sales Pipeline
5. Activities & Follow-ups
6. Consulting Projects
7. Team & Assignments
8. Reports & Analytics
9. Documents
10. Notifications
11. Settings

Display navigation items according to the logged-in user's permissions.

---

5. MODULE ONE: EXECUTIVE DASHBOARD

This is the first screen users see after logging in.

Build a dynamic dashboard that displays relevant information based on user role.

FOUNDER / ADMIN DASHBOARD

At the top, display summary KPI cards:

- Total Inquiries.
- New Inquiries This Month.
- Active Prospects.
- Qualified Leads.
- Active Opportunities.
- Total Clients.
- Active Consulting Projects.
- Closed Deals.
- Total Deal Value.
- Outstanding Follow-ups.

Include date filters:

- Today.
- Last 7 Days.
- Last 30 Days.
- This Month.
- Last Month.
- This Quarter.
- This Year.
- Custom Date Range.

DASHBOARD VISUALISATIONS

Create the following charts:

1. Inquiry Growth Chart

Display incoming inquiries over time.

2. Lead Conversion Funnel

Show the number of prospects moving through the sales pipeline.

3. Sales Pipeline Overview

Display the value of opportunities at each stage.

4. Revenue and Deal Performance

Display closed-won deal value over time.

5. Team Performance

Compare the activities and results of individual BD managers and sales representatives.

6. Inquiry Sources

Show where business inquiries originate:

- Website.
- Referral.
- LinkedIn.
- WhatsApp.
- Facebook.
- Direct Outreach.
- Events.
- Other.

7. Consulting Project Overview

Show:

- Not Started.
- Planning.
- In Progress.
- Under Review.
- Completed.
- On Hold.

RECENT ACTIVITY FEED

Display recent events, including:

- New inquiries.
- New contacts.
- Lead assignments.
- Stage changes.
- Follow-up activities.
- New deals.
- New client engagements.
- Consultant assignments.
- Project updates.

Each activity should show the user responsible and timestamp.

MY WORK TODAY

Include a section showing:

- My assigned leads.
- Follow-ups due today.
- Overdue follow-ups.
- Upcoming meetings.
- Active deals.
- Pending tasks.

All dashboard figures must come from real database records. Never populate the live dashboard with invented statistics.

---

6. MODULE TWO: INQUIRY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

This is one of the most important modules.

The company currently receives inquiries through its public website.

These inquiries are submitted through forms and stored in Google Sheets, while supporting documents and business diagnostic files are uploaded to Google Drive.

AffluentOS must centralise and manage these submissions.

INQUIRY CATEGORIES

Support multiple types of inquiries:

1. Business Audit Requests.
2. Custom Business Consulting.
3. Business Advisory.
4. Business Strategy Requests.
5. Business Growth Support.
6. Business Development Requests.
7. Partnership Inquiries.
8. General Business Inquiries.

Make inquiry categories configurable by the administrator.

INQUIRY DATABASE

Each inquiry should have a unique system-generated reference number.

Example: AA-INQ-2026-0001.

Store the following information:

Client information

- Full name.
- Business name.
- Email address.
- Phone number.
- WhatsApp number.
- Business location.
- Industry.
- Website or social media link.

Business information

- Business description.
- Business stage.
- Team size.
- Business model.
- Annual revenue range, if supplied.
- Current challenges.
- Business objectives.

Inquiry information

- Inquiry category.
- Requested service.
- Description of support required.
- Specific questions.
- Expected outcomes.
- Budget range, if supplied.
- Preferred consultation method.
- Date submitted.
- Source of inquiry.

Supporting documents

- Business pitch decks.
- Diagnostic reports.
- Financial documents.
- Business plans.
- Other uploaded files.

Internal management fields

- Assigned BD manager.
- Assigned sales representative.
- Assigned consultant.
- Inquiry status.
- Priority.
- Internal notes.
- Last contact date.
- Next follow-up date.
- Conversion outcome.

INQUIRY STATUS

Create the following statuses:

- New.
- Unreviewed.
- Under Review.
- Contacted.
- Awaiting Client Response.
- Qualified.
- Proposal Requested.
- Converted.
- Not Qualified.
- Closed / Lost.
- Archived.

Allow administrators to customise the statuses.

INQUIRY MANAGEMENT INTERFACE

Create two views:

Table View

Display:

- Reference number.
- Client name.
- Business name.
- Inquiry type.
- Submission date.
- Source.
- Assigned BD manager.
- Status.
- Priority.
- Next action.

Include search, filters, sorting, pagination, and bulk assignment.

Kanban View

Create a drag-and-drop board showing inquiries grouped by status.

Allow authorised users to move inquiries between stages.

Record every status change in the activity history.

INQUIRY DETAIL PAGE

When a user opens an inquiry, display a comprehensive profile with tabs:

1. Overview.
2. Business Information.
3. Uploaded Documents.
4. Activities.
5. Internal Notes.
6. Assignment History.

Include quick actions:

- Assign BD Manager.
- Assign Sales Representative.
- Assign Consultant.
- Create Contact.
- Create Deal.
- Schedule Follow-up.
- Add Note.
- Change Status.
- Convert to Client.

IMPORTANT:

An inquiry should not automatically become a client simply because someone submits a form.

The system must support a proper qualification and conversion process.

---

7. MODULE THREE: GOOGLE SHEETS AND GOOGLE DRIVE INTEGRATION

This is a critical requirement.

The existing website already has a functioning inquiry collection process.

Do not break or replace this process without a deliberate migration plan.

GOOGLE SHEETS INTEGRATION

Connect AffluentOS to the existing Google Sheets containing website inquiry submissions.

Requirements:

- Authenticate using secure Google OAuth.
- Allow the administrator to select the Google account.
- Allow the administrator to select the existing spreadsheet.
- Allow selection of the specific worksheet.
- Map existing spreadsheet columns to AffluentOS database fields.
- Import existing inquiries.
- Automatically synchronise new submissions.
- Avoid duplicate records.
- Track synchronisation status.
- Display failed synchronisations.
- Allow manual synchronisation.

Implement an initial historical import so existing inquiries are not lost.

GOOGLE DRIVE INTEGRATION

Connect to the existing Google Drive folder where website submissions and attachments are stored.

Requirements:

- Authenticate with appropriate Google permissions.
- Allow selection of the existing folder.
- Retrieve the relevant uploaded files.
- Match documents to their corresponding inquiry.
- Display documents inside the inquiry profile.
- Allow authorised users to preview or download files.
- Preserve the original Google Drive file references.
- Display file name, type, upload date, and size.
- Handle missing or inaccessible files gracefully.

Do not expose public Drive links.

Documents must only be accessible to authorised users.

SYNCHRONISATION ARCHITECTURE

Use AffluentOS as the central operational database.

The preferred workflow:

Website Form → Google Sheets / Google Drive → AffluentOS → Team Management.

Also support a future direct website-to-AffluentOS API integration.

For new submissions, use a reliable webhook or scheduled synchronisation mechanism.

Requirements:

- Idempotent data imports.
- Duplicate detection.
- Retry failed synchronisations.
- Sync logs.
- Error notifications.
- Last successful sync timestamp.
- Manual resync.

Do not rely on a browser session or a user's personal Google login to keep synchronisation working in the background.

Use a secure server-side integration with appropriately authorised credentials.

---

8. MODULE FOUR: CRM / CONTACT MANAGEMENT

Build a proper centralised CRM.

Every business, founder, prospect, client, partner, and professional relationship should have a contact record.

CONTACT TYPES

- Prospect.
- Qualified Lead.
- Active Client.
- Former Client.
- Business Partner.
- Strategic Partner.
- Referral Partner.
- Other.

CONTACT PROFILE

Each contact should have:

Personal details:

- Full name.
- Email.
- Phone.
- WhatsApp.
- LinkedIn profile.
- Location.

Business details:

- Business name.
- Industry.
- Website.
- Business size.
- Business stage.
- Business description.

Relationship details:

- Contact type.
- Relationship owner.
- Acquisition source.
- First contact date.
- Last interaction.
- Next follow-up.
- Relationship status.

CONTACT TIMELINE

Create a chronological interaction history:

- First inquiry.
- Calls.
- Meetings.
- Emails.
- WhatsApp interactions recorded manually.
- Proposals sent.
- Follow-ups.
- Notes.
- Deals created.
- Services purchased.
- Projects completed.

Users should be able to see the entire relationship history without searching through multiple spreadsheets.

DUPLICATE DETECTION

Prevent duplicate contact records using:

- Email address.
- Phone number.
- Business name.

When a potential duplicate is identified, alert the user and provide a merge option for authorised users.

Allow multiple contacts to be associated with the same business organisation.

---

9. MODULE FIVE: SALES PIPELINE AND DEAL MANAGEMENT

Create a visual sales CRM similar to Pipedrive or HubSpot.

This should help the company monitor every business opportunity from initial contact to closing.

DEFAULT SALES PIPELINE

Create these stages:

1. New Lead

A prospect has been identified or submitted an inquiry.

2. Initial Contact

The BD representative has reached out.

3. Discovery / Needs Assessment

The team is understanding the business, its challenges, requirements, and expectations.

4. Qualified Opportunity

The prospect has a genuine need, interest, and potential to become a client.

5. Consultation / Meeting Scheduled

A meeting or consultation has been scheduled.

6. Proposal / Service Recommendation

A proposal or recommended service package has been presented.

7. Negotiation / Follow-up

The team is discussing pricing, scope, expectations, or terms.

8. Closed Won

The client has agreed to proceed.

9. Closed Lost

The opportunity did not convert.

Allow the administrator to create custom pipelines and modify stages.

DEAL RECORD

Each deal should include:

- Deal title.
- Associated contact.
- Associated business.
- Linked inquiry.
- Deal owner.
- Supporting team members.
- Service category.
- Deal value.
- Currency.
- Probability of conversion.
- Expected closing date.
- Current pipeline stage.
- Next action.
- Next follow-up date.
- Proposal document.
- Internal notes.
- Lost reason.
- Date created.
- Date closed.

Support NGN and other currencies.

PIPELINE BOARD

Create a drag-and-drop Kanban interface.

Each column represents a sales stage.

Each deal card should display:

- Deal name.
- Business name.
- Deal value.
- Assigned representative.
- Expected closing date.
- Priority.
- Last activity.

Display the total value of deals in each stage.

SALES PIPELINE METRICS

Calculate:

- Total pipeline value.
- Weighted pipeline value.
- Open opportunities.
- Won deals.
- Lost deals.
- Win rate.
- Average deal value.
- Average sales cycle.
- Conversion rate between stages.
- Deals closing this month.

LOST DEAL ANALYSIS

Whenever a deal is marked Closed Lost, require a reason.

Default reasons:

- Budget constraints.
- No response.
- Chose competitor.
- Not ready.
- Service mismatch.
- Timing.
- Price objections.
- Other.

Use this information for future sales analysis.

---

10. MODULE SIX: BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITY MANAGEMENT

Build a dedicated workspace for BD managers and sales representatives.

This is where team members record the relationships they develop and their daily business development activities.

NEW LEAD FORM

Allow BD managers to create new leads manually.

Fields:

- Contact name.
- Business name.
- Email.
- Phone.
- Industry.
- Location.
- Website.
- Source of lead.
- Service of interest.
- Business challenge.
- Estimated opportunity value.
- Assigned representative.
- Lead priority.
- Initial notes.
- Next follow-up date.

Automatically associate the record with the logged-in user as its creator.

Allow reassignment by authorised users.

ACTIVITY LOG

Team members should be able to record:

- Phone calls.
- WhatsApp conversations.
- Emails.
- Discovery meetings.
- Follow-up messages.
- Client visits.
- Networking events.
- Proposal submissions.
- Other interactions.

Every activity should have:

- Activity type.
- Contact or deal.
- Date and time.
- Summary.
- Outcome.
- Next action.
- Next follow-up date.
- User responsible.

FOLLOW-UP MANAGEMENT

Create a follow-up workspace.

Display:

- Follow-ups due today.
- Upcoming follow-ups.
- Overdue follow-ups.
- Completed follow-ups.

Allow users to mark follow-ups as completed.

If a follow-up is completed, allow the user to record the outcome and schedule another one.

Create notification reminders for overdue and upcoming follow-ups.

BD PERFORMANCE DASHBOARD

Each BD manager should see:

- Leads generated.
- Leads contacted.
- Qualified leads.
- Discovery meetings.
- Proposals submitted.
- Deals won.
- Deals lost.
- Total closed deal value.
- Conversion rate.
- Follow-ups completed.
- Outstanding follow-ups.

The founder should be able to compare performance across all representatives.

Distinguish between activity metrics and actual sales outcomes. Do not reward meaningless activity counts without tracking conversion quality.

---

11. MODULE SEVEN: CONSULTANT AND BUSINESS ANALYST ASSIGNMENT

Create a system for assigning consultants and analysts to specific clients, business audits, and consulting engagements.

CONSULTANT DIRECTORY

Each consultant profile should include:

- Full name.
- Email.
- Phone.
- Professional title.
- Specialisation.
- Skills.
- Experience level.
- Availability status.
- Active projects.
- Completed projects.
- Current workload.
- Profile photograph.
- Short professional biography.

CONSULTANT SPECIALISATIONS

Allow multiple specialisations:

- Business Strategy.
- Business Analysis.
- Financial Analysis.
- Market Research.
- Business Development.
- Marketing Strategy.
- Operations.
- Process Improvement.
- Sales Strategy.
- Business Model Development.

Allow administrators to add more specialisations.

ASSIGNMENT PROCESS

When a business audit or consulting inquiry is qualified, authorised users should be able to create a consulting engagement.

The assignment form should include:

- Client.
- Business.
- Related inquiry.
- Engagement type.
- Scope of work.
- Required expertise.
- Lead consultant.
- Supporting consultant.
- Assigned analyst.
- Project deadline.
- Priority.
- Deliverables.
- Internal instructions.

Support multiple consultants and analysts on one engagement.

ASSIGNMENT WORKFLOW

Inquiry received → Qualified → Consultant selection → Assignment approved → Project created → Work commenced → Report submitted → Client delivery → Completed.

Allow the founder or authorised administrator to approve consultant assignments.

WORKLOAD MANAGEMENT

Create a dashboard showing:

- Available consultants.
- Consultants currently assigned.
- Active engagements.
- Pending assignments.
- Overloaded team members.
- Completed projects.

The system should help management distribute work fairly.

---

12. MODULE EIGHT: CLIENT AND CONSULTING PROJECT MANAGEMENT

Once a deal is closed won and a client engagement is confirmed, create a consulting project.

PROJECT RECORD

Include:

- Project name.
- Client.
- Associated deal.
- Project reference.
- Engagement type.
- Project description.
- Scope of work.
- Start date.
- Expected completion date.
- Project owner.
- Lead consultant.
- Supporting analysts.
- Project status.
- Agreed fee.
- Deliverables.
- Internal documents.

PROJECT STATUS

- Not Started.
- Planning.
- In Progress.
- Awaiting Client Input.
- Under Review.
- Completed.
- On Hold.
- Cancelled.

PROJECT TASK MANAGEMENT

Allow project managers to create tasks and assign them to consultants and analysts.

Each task should include:

- Task title.
- Description.
- Assigned person.
- Due date.
- Priority.
- Status.
- Supporting files.
- Comments.

PROJECT PROGRESS

Display:

- Task completion percentage.
- Milestones.
- Pending deliverables.
- Overdue tasks.
- Project activity.
- Upcoming deadlines.

DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT

Allow team members to upload:

- Business audit reports.
- Consulting reports.
- Research documents.
- Client presentations.
- Proposals.
- Business diagnostic documents.
- Final deliverables.

Maintain document version history where possible.

Use secure document access and record who uploaded or downloaded sensitive documents.

---

13. MODULE NINE: REPORTS AND BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE

Create a comprehensive analytics section for the founder and management.

The platform should turn operational data into actionable business intelligence.

INQUIRY ANALYTICS

- Total inquiries received.
- Inquiry growth over time.
- Inquiries by service category.
- Inquiries by industry.
- Inquiries by location.
- Inquiry source performance.
- Inquiry-to-qualified-lead conversion.

SALES ANALYTICS

- Pipeline value.
- Closed deal value.
- Monthly sales performance.
- Quarterly sales performance.
- Deal conversion rates.
- Sales cycle duration.
- Average deal size.
- Lost opportunity analysis.

TEAM ANALYTICS

- Leads generated per BD manager.
- Opportunities managed.
- Meetings conducted.
- Proposals submitted.
- Deals won.
- Revenue attributed to team members.
- Follow-up completion.
- Individual conversion rates.

CONSULTING ANALYTICS

- Number of active projects.
- Number of completed projects.
- Projects by service category.
- Consultant utilisation.
- Average project completion time.
- Outstanding deliverables.
- Project profitability, where cost data is available.

EXPORTS

Allow authorised users to export:

- Inquiry reports.
- Contact databases.
- Sales pipeline reports.
- Team performance reports.
- Client reports.
- Project reports.

Support CSV and Excel exports.

Include date filters and report-generation timestamps.

---

14. MODULE TEN: INTERNAL NOTES, NOTIFICATIONS AND COLLABORATION

The application should allow the team to collaborate around individual inquiries, contacts, deals, and projects.

INTERNAL NOTES

Users can add internal notes to records.

Notes should include:

- Author.
- Timestamp.
- Related record.
- Note content.

Allow @mentions where practical.

NOTIFICATIONS

Create an in-app notification centre.

Notify users when:

- A new inquiry is received.
- A lead is assigned.
- An inquiry is reassigned.
- A follow-up is due.
- A deal changes stage.
- A new task is assigned.
- A project deadline approaches.
- A consultant is assigned.
- A project is updated.

Users should be able to mark notifications as read.

Allow notification preferences.

ACTIVITY HISTORY

Every important change must be recorded in an audit trail.

Track:

- Who created a record.
- Who edited a record.
- Who changed a status.
- Who assigned a lead.
- Who reassigned a consultant.
- When a deal was closed.
- When a project was completed.

The founder and authorised administrators should be able to review these events.

---

15. DATABASE ARCHITECTURE

Use a relational database, preferably PostgreSQL through Supabase.

Create properly related tables.

Suggested database entities:

1. users
2. roles
3. permissions
4. user_roles
5. organisations
6. contacts
7. inquiries
8. inquiry_documents
9. lead_assignments
10. pipelines
11. pipeline_stages
12. deals
13. deal_contacts
14. activities
15. follow_ups
16. consultants
17. consultant_skills
18. engagements
19. engagement_assignments
20. projects
21. project_tasks
22. project_milestones
23. documents
24. notes
25. notifications
26. audit_logs
27. integrations
28. sync_logs
29. services
30. lost_reasons

Use UUIDs for internal primary keys.

Every relevant record should contain:

- created_at
- updated_at
- created_by
- updated_by

Maintain proper foreign keys, indexes, constraints, and data validation.

Use soft deletion for important business records where appropriate, with recovery and administrative controls.

Avoid creating duplicate records when importing data from Google Sheets.

DATABASE SECURITY

Implement Supabase Row Level Security.

Examples:

- BD managers can access their assigned leads.
- Sales representatives can access their authorised opportunities.
- Consultants can access assigned projects and related client information.
- Administrators can access records within their authorised scope.
- Super admins can access all company records.

All sensitive operations must be validated server-side.

---

16. TECHNOLOGY STACK

Preferred technology:

Frontend:

- Next.js or React.
- TypeScript.
- Tailwind CSS.
- shadcn/ui.
- Recharts for analytics.
- TanStack Table for data tables.

Backend:

- Supabase.
- PostgreSQL.
- Supabase Authentication.
- Supabase Storage.
- Secure server-side API endpoints.

Integrations:

- Google Sheets API.
- Google Drive API.
- Google OAuth.
- Email notification integration.
- WhatsApp integration as a future extension.

Deployment:

- Vercel or another reliable hosting platform.
- Supabase hosted database.

Ensure that secrets and API credentials are stored securely in server-side environment variables.

Never expose Google credentials, service role keys, or other secrets in frontend code.

---

17. APPLICATION SETTINGS

Create a settings area for administrators.

Include:

- Company profile.
- Company logo.
- Team management.
- User roles.
- Permissions.
- Inquiry categories.
- Inquiry statuses.
- Sales pipelines.
- Sales stages.
- Service categories.
- Lead sources.
- Consultant specialisations.
- Project statuses.
- Notification preferences.
- Google integrations.
- Data import/export.
- Audit logs.

Make the system configurable without modifying source code.

---

18. KEY AUTOMATIONS

Build these automation rules:

1. When a website inquiry is received, automatically create an inquiry record.

2. Generate a unique inquiry reference number.

3. Notify the admin of new submissions.

4. Allow automatic assignment based on configurable rules, such as inquiry type, workload, or round-robin distribution.

5. Notify the assigned BD manager.

6. When an inquiry becomes qualified, allow creation of a deal.

7. When a deal becomes Closed Won, prompt the user to create a client engagement.

8. When a consulting project is created, notify assigned consultants.

9. When a follow-up date arrives, notify the responsible representative.

10. When a follow-up becomes overdue, highlight it on the dashboard.

11. When a project deadline approaches, notify the project owner.

12. When a project is completed, update the consulting analytics.

13. Record all automated actions in the audit trail.

Automations must be configurable and should not silently change critical business records without an authorised rule.

---

19. CRITICAL USER EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

The platform must be genuinely usable by a growing team.

Prioritise:

- Fast search across contacts, businesses, inquiries, and deals.
- Global search.
- Filters and saved views.
- Bulk record assignment.
- Easy lead creation.
- One-click follow-up logging.
- Quick status changes.
- Clear overdue indicators.
- Easy document access.
- Useful dashboard summaries.
- Minimal unnecessary clicks.

Every record should have a consistent detail page.

Make the system usable by non-technical team members.

Provide useful empty states when no data exists.

Display loading indicators and meaningful error messages.

---

20. DEVELOPMENT PHASES

Build the application in manageable phases.

PHASE 1: FOUNDATION

- Application branding.
- Authentication.

To automatically pull inquiries from your existing Google Forms and Google Sheets into AffluentOS:

   - Paste the webhook script provided in the in-app **Production Guide** (`Code.gs`).
   - Add a trigger: **`onFormSubmit`** ➔ **Event Source: From spreadsheet** ➔ **Event type: On form submit**.

3. **Two-Way Synchronization:**
   - AffluentOS includes a manual **Sync Now** button and an automated polling interval (`5m`, `15m`, `1h`) to fetch new submissions or changes made directly in the spreadsheet.
